findings.issue: This is the deploy-settings description of VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, read from deploy/aws/config.example.env. It says 'Blank in a non-prod environment: a keypair is generated on first start.' The AWS Helm chart always sets SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod (templates/deployment.yaml:76), and PushService.initKeys never generates keys under prod. On the AWS deploy, which is the only user of this table, a blank value therefore always turns web push off. The non-prod sentence does not apply there and could make an operator think leaving it blank is fine. config.example.env:63 already says it correctly: 'Blank = web push off in production.'
findings.fix: Reword to: 'Browser-push (VAPID) public key for notification-service, base64url (npx web-push generate-vapid-keys). Optional: blank turns web push off on AWS (prod profile never generates keys). Keep the pair stable; a new pair invalidates every subscription.' Then regenerate the md with env-reference.mjs.

findings.issue: isSecretSetting does not exclude PUBLIC the way isSecret does on line 115. The deploy table (environment-variables.md:233) therefore marks VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY with the lock icon and hides its default, although it is a public key. This is cosmetic.
findings.fix: Add PUBLIC to the exclusion regex in isSecretSetting, or leave it and track it as follow-up.
